repositories.readme:
# Agent Substrate **Zero-trust sandboxing for millions of agents on Kubernetes.** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/agent-substrate/substrate)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml?query=branch%3Amain) [![govulncheck](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/agent-substrate/substrate?style=flat)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/stargazers) [Quickstart](#quickstart-development) · [Security](docs/security/security.md) · [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
## What is Agent Substrate? Agent Substrate is a security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. Purpose-built for the era of autonomous agents, Substrate delivers fast resume operations in less than 500ms, with more than 500 activations per second. Agents get isolated compute, identity, networking, and storage. Sensitive credentials are kept out of reach from untrusted code. It supports multiple sandbox technologies, including microVMs and gVisor, while enabling a consistent lifecycle and management of all sandboxes. At its core, Agent Substrate maps a larger set of “actors” (stateful workloads such as agents) onto a smaller pool of ready “workers”. Because agents spend most of their lives waiting on models, tools, or humans, Substrate snapshots idle actors out of memory and restores them when a request arrives. Substrate is a low-opinion runtime, not an agent SDK. The workloads it runs do not have to be AI agents, though autonomous, untrusted, mostly-idle agents are the target for its isolation and scheduling model. It runs on standard Kubernetes: Pods, autoscaling, NetworkPolicies. It adds agent-specific scheduling, snapshotting, identity, and network mediation. This allows agentic, inference, training, and reinforcement learning workloads to share one infrastructure plane. ## Security Model Substrate treats every actor as untrusted and mutually hostile, so tenants can share physical nodes without sharing a security boundary. Every control operates within the cold-start and resume budget. See the [Security Guide](docs/security/security.md) for the full list of security principles and threat model. * **Always sandboxed, VM-grade boundaries:** Every actor runs inside a dedicated [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/) (`runsc`) or [Cloud Hypervisor](https://www.cloudhypervisor.org/) microVM sandbox with segregated compute, network, and storage. Plain Linux containers are not supported. * **Per-agent cryptographic identity:** Every active actor receives a short-lived [SPIFFE](https://spiffe.io/) X.509 certificate by default, and the egress gateway can mint per-actor JWTs on demand when an egress policy calls for one. Both carry the actor identity and atespace (the Substrate namespace grouping), and are designed to federate with external identity systems. * **Zero credentials in the sandbox:** Actors never hold actor identity JWTs/certs, API keys, or cloud tokens. The built-in egress gateway ([`atenet-egress`](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md)) injects credentials into approved outbound requests outside the sandbox, so a prompt-injected or compromised agent has nothing to exfiltrate. * **Default-deny networking:** Actors start with a private network stack, no inbound path except through the ingress router (`atenet-router`), no lateral actor-to-actor or control-plane access, and outbound traffic [restricted by the egress gateway](docs/guides/egress-traffic.md). * **Pluggable policy at the edge:** The egress gateway acts as an external Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) that is fully replaceable, allowing you to attach your own authorization, DLP, prompt-injection scanning, or cloud IAM policy engine without placing policy code inside the untrusted sandbox. ## Performance & Multiplexing [![Agent Substrate Demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/ZEzkCFJkzjY/hq1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEzkCFJkzjY) *Watch the Agent Substrate cluster multiplex ~250 stateful actors across just 8 physical pods.* This demo highlights the core developer experience and "Agentic Infrastructure" capabilities of Substrate: 1. **Actor Teleport:** Suspend and resume actors onto any available worker in the pool, when needed. 2. **Full-State Persistence:** Working memory (RAM) and filesystem state are captured in snapshots and restored intact across hibernation cycles, without losing in-flight sessions or tool state. 3. **10x–30x Oversubscription:** Multiplex a large registry of stateful actors onto a small pool of warm worker pods, paying for compute only while an agent is actively thinking or executing a tool. To reproduce this demo in your own cluster, see the **[Counter Demo](demos/counter/README.md)**. For more walkthroughs, visit the **[agent-substrate YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN9PPqlTtVxlcpbQ-NWpfZQ)**. ## Star History ## Framework Agnostic & Compatibility Agent Substrate is **framework and agent harness agnostic**. Because it runs standard OCI container images inside gVisor or microVM sandboxes and enforces security outside the workload, it hosts agents built on any stack without SDK changes: * **Agent Development Kit (ADK):** Preserves session state across invocations as actor state. * **LangChain:** Drop-in execution environment for LangChain agents and tool calls. * **Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity:** High-density, stateful coding environments that keep system and filesystem state across sessions while isolating untrusted code execution. * **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** Deploy sandboxed MCP servers as Substrate Actors with per-actor identity and egress controls. ## Ecosystem & Examples * **[Agent Executor](https://github.com/google/ax):** A distributed agent runtime that demonstrates building a secure, hyper-scalable agent harness on Agent Substrate (see the [announcement blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/agent-executor-googles-distributed-agent-runtime) and [integration guide](https://github.com/google/ax#2-deploy-the-control-plane)). * **[kagent](https://github.com/kagent-dev/kagent):** A CNCF Sandbox project and Kubernetes-native framework for building, deploying, and managing AI agents that uses Agent Substrate to run sandboxed, stateful agent workloads (see the [announcement blog](https://kagent.dev/blog/the-future-of-kagent)). ## Status and compatibility Agent Substrate has reached 1.0. We are committed to compatibility and stability of the public API, CLI, and configuration formats. We will continue to add new features, but we will not break existing APIs or configuration formats without a major version bump. See "Compatibility and schema evolution" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details. ### Supported Kubernetes Releases Currently we aim to support the [latest stable release](https://kubernetes.io/releases/) of Kubernetes, and the previous minor release. ## Community For announcements, technical discussions, and community support, please join the **[ate-dev](https://groups.google.com/g/ate-dev)** Google Group. We host a weekly community meeting every Thursday from 10:00am - 11:00am PST. - Video call link: https://meet.google.com/uhq-cxvn-dhy - Or dial: (US) +1 253-289-6971 PIN: 787 664 574 59# - More phone numbers: https://tel.meet/uhq-cxvn-dhy?pin=9044088223662 - [Meeting notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1obSIvfcafLNniLYTQCcT2eCgxHqa2AQ3Ga7YTsju49s) for the weekly sync meeting - [Recordings and transcripts](https://drive.google.com/corp/drive/u/0/folders/1rX1S6vPxPrR8dA1lEBuBEXkGKjHtG-mL) of all community meetings We also have channels in the CNCF slack; [request an invite here](https://slack.cncf.io/) if you don't have access. - [#substrate-users](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6RCAJULW) to discuss using substrate. - [#substrate-dev](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6M3E2J3D) to discuss developing substrate. ## Developing Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on contributing to the project. We welcome contributions of all kinds, but the project is VERY young. Our immediate focus is on building out the core system and demos, so we may not be able to review or merge contributions that don't align with those goals in the near term. ## Quickstart (Development) To quickly set up the complete environment: 1. Make sure you have [Go](https://go.dev/doc/install), [`kubectl`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/), and [`docker`](https://www.docker.com/) installed and configured on your dev machine. We will automatically manage other dependencies via Go, including [`kind`](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/). A Linux host that will run more than about a thousand sandboxes also needs a larger kernel neighbor table (`net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1/2/3` = 4096/16384/32768); `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh` warns when the host is at the default of 1024. 2. Run the following steps: ```shell # create cluster and local registry hack/create-kind-cluster.sh # make ate-setup target the kind cluster; set this in every shell that runs # ate-setup, including for the demo walkthroughs export ATE_INSTALL_KIND=true # install Substrate go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy ate-system --credential-provider='{"name":"k8s.io"}' \ --ingress-allowed-spiffe-ids=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/ate-system/sa/atenet-client # install counter demo go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy demo counter # install kubectl-ate go install ./cmd/kubectl-ate # create a counter actor in the demo's atespace (--template names the # actor template, resolved in the actor's atespace) kubectl ate create actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter --template counter # serve a local proxy on port 8000 that sends requests to the actor through the # network router kubectl ate proxy actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `{"name":"k8s.io"}` deploys the bundled credential provider with an empty, > default-deny namespace policy. Before an actor can have a credential > injected, grant its atespace the namespaces whose Secrets it may read; see > [Enable it](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md#enable-it). 3. In a **separate terminal**, send an HTTP request to increment the counter: ```shell curl -X POST -i http://localhost:8000/ ``` ### Custom Setup and Deployment You can deploy or cleanup specific Agent Substrate components using the installation script. See `go run ./cmd/ate-setup` for all options. ```bash # Re-deploy only ate-apiserver of the ATE system go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy apiserver # Delete everything (core system and all demos) go run ./cmd/ate-setup delete all ``` ### Tearing down local `kind` resources If you need to delete the local `kind` cluster and its registry (if it was created by `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh`): ```bash ./hack/delete-kind-cluster.sh ``` ### GKE Quickstart To deploy on Google Kubernetes Engine, follow the official [GKE Installation Guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/ai-ml/install-overview-substrate). It lists the prerequisites and gives the one-line installer command. The installer's source and detailed options are in [substrate-gke](https://github.com/ai-on-gke/substrate-gke). ## Demos We provide several sample applications demonstrating Agent Substrate's capabilities: 1. **[Counter Demo](demos/counter/README.md)**: A stateful Go HTTP server demonstrating state preservation across suspends/resumes, and on-demand actor resumption and routing via the Substrate router. 2. **[Sandbox Demo (Antigravity)](demos/sandbox/README.md)**: A secure, sandboxed execution environment (running Alpine Linux) that allows arbitrary shell execution while preserving filesystem state across sessions. 3. **[Claude Code Multiplex](demos/claude-code-multiplex/README.md)**: Demonstrates oversubscribing physical hardware by multiplexing multiple Claude Code agents onto a limited pool of workers. 4. **[Multi-Template](demos/multi-template/README.md)**: Two `ActorTemplate`s running different binaries share one `WorkerPool`, even though the templates live in different atespaces. 5. **[Request Parking](demos/parking/README.md)**: An oversubscribed pool where the router holds inbound requests until a worker frees up, instead of returning `503`. ### Documentation & Guides * [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md): How the control plane, node supervisor, and networking stack fit together. * [API Configuration Guide](docs/reference/api-guide.md): Detailed reference for configuring WorkerPools, ActorTemplates, Secrets, and Volumes. * [Full CLI Documentation](docs/reference/kubectl-ate.md): Installation and usage for `kubectl-ate`. * [Glossary](docs/reference/glossary.md): Core terms (Actor, Atespace, ActorTemplate, WorkerPool, Worker, ate-api-server, atenet, atelet, ateworker) and how they relate. * [Integration Repositories](docs/project/integration-repos.md): Where integrations live, how their repositories are named, and how fixes flow back to core. * [Observability Guide](docs/guides/observability.md): Guide to actor logging, metrics, and distributed tracing. * [Extending Substrate](docs/security/extensibility.md): How to augment or replace the built-in ingress and egress gateways. * [Authentication Guide](docs/guides/authentication.md): Which credential people, pods and CI jobs should use with the Substrate API, and how to trust more JWT issuers. * [Actor JWTs](docs/guides/actor-jwts.md): What an actor JWT contains, how relying parties verify it, and how to rotate the signing key. * [Federating actor JWTs](docs/guides/actor-jwt-federation.md): Serve the actor JWT issuer publicly and set up a relying party outside the cluster to trust it. * [Rotating the actor JWT signing key](docs/guides/actor-jwt-key-rotation.md): The rotation steps, how long to wait between them, and replacing a compromised key. * [Egress Traffic](docs/guides/egress-traffic.md): Which protocols an Actor may reach the outside world with and which are blocked. * [Enabling man-in-the-middle (MITM) interception for Actor Egress policy](docs/guides/egress-trust-bundle.md): Egress policies such as header injection depend on MITM interception of Actor traffic. This guide explains how an Actor should be configured to enable interception. * [Request Parking](docs/concepts/request-parking.md): How the router parks requests through transient worker-pool saturation. * [Sandbox Asset Cache](docs/concepts/sandbox-asset-cache.md): How a node caches the sandbox binaries actors run on, decides which runtimes it needs, and evicts to a budget. * [Upgrade Runbook](docs/guides/upgrade.md): Upgrade a running install to a newer supported release, and roll back if needed. * [Node Storage](docs/guides/node-storage.md): How to give snapshot I/O its own disk. * [Security Guide](docs/security/security.md): Security overview, security principles, and threat modeling. * [Benchmarking Guide](docs/guides/benchmarking.md): Locust-based load tests, monitoring stack, and the orchestrated benchmark harness. ## Tour ### Commands * `cmd/ateapi`: The core control plane API server exposing gRPC endpoints to manage actor and worker lifecycles. * `cmd/atelet`: A node-level DaemonSet that supervises physical worker pods, coordinates snapshotting, and manages state transfers. * `cmd/atecontroller`: A Kubernetes controller that reconciles WorkerPool custom resources. * `cmd/ate-idp-server`: Serves the OpenID discovery document and key set that relying parties use to verify actor JWTs. * `cmd/atenet`: A combined networking controller providing Envoy routing and proxy sidecars. * `cmd/ateworker-gvisor`: An interior-pod helper running inside sandboxed worker pods to execute `runsc` checkpoint and restore commands. * `cmd/ateworker-microvm`: The microVM peer of `ateworker-gvisor`, running actors as cloud-hypervisor VMs. * `cmd/podcertcontroller`: A "polyfill" that provides Pod Certificate signers that will eventually ship in upstream Kubernetes (with different names). * `cmd/kubectl-ate`: A CLI tool for managing Agent Substrate resources. See its [README](docs/reference/kubectl-ate.md). * `cmd/benchmarking`: Synthetic workloads used by the load tests, including `glutton`, which consumes RAM, disk, and file descriptors on demand. * `demos/`: Sample applications demonstrating Agent Substrate capabilities.

repositories.description: WorkBuddy、CodeBuddy 桌面端增强助手：签到猫猫旅行成长计划查询、多账号独立备份、点切即用；免打扰模式让 AI 无人值守跑长任务；跨账号会话迁移、异常中断自动续接；暂存/快捷提示词；毛玻璃主题与更多实用功能。
repositories.readme:
WorkDaddy

**语言：** [简体中文](README.md) · [English](README_en.md) · [日本語](README_ja.md) > **WorkDaddy 是 WorkBuddy 和 CodeBuddy 桌面端增强助手：多账号独立备份、点切即用，跨账号会话迁移、模型管理与自动化任务。WorkBuddy 还支持免打扰、异常中断自动续接、暂存/快捷提示词和五种主题。账号与配置全部留在本机。** > 本机回环 CDP 注入 · 不改官方安装包。 一个基于 **Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)** 的 [WorkBuddy](https://www.workbuddy.cn/)、[WorkBuddy AI](https://www.workbuddy.ai/)、[CodeBuddy CN](https://www.codebuddy.cn/) 和 [CodeBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.ai/) 桌面端增强工具。 CodeBuddy 支持范围为 **Electron 智能体窗口**，不包含 VS Code 编辑器模式的增强面板。通过本机调试接口连接运行中的客户端，不修改官方安装包或签名。 ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blueviolet) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%2011%2B%20%7C%20Windows%2010%2F11%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522.13-green) --- ## 💖 赞助商 > 想出现在这里？欢迎[联系我们](mailto:richdaddycashmany@163.com)。
Nagora 是专为开发者和团队打造的多模型 AI API 网关。通过一个账户和一枚 API Key，即可统一调用 26+ 款主流文本与图像模型，兼容 OpenAI、Anthropic 与 Gemini 协议，并可无缝接入 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 等开发工具。平台提供智能路由、自动故障转移、透明计费与统一账单，同时支持预算、限速、并发控制，让个人开发、团队协作和生产环境中的 AI 调用更稳定、更可控。无需改造现有应用，只需替换 Base URL 与 API Key，最快 1 分钟即可完成接入。
--- #### 它能做什么 - **方便切换账号**：每个客户端的账号独立备份，点一下就切，再也不用每次扫码。 - **无感登录新账号**：「登录新账号」支持免退出 OAuth 授权——不退出 WorkBuddy，在浏览器完成扫码后新账号自动加入列表；也可选传统的「假退出」方式回登录页扫码。 - **账号导入导出**：把全部账号备份加密导出，在另一台电脑安装 WorkDaddy 后一键导入，方便电脑之间迁移账号。 - **成长计划与活跃状态**：国内版账号页查询成长任务进度、当日签到和活跃状态、连续活跃天数，以及 Buddy 解锁和旅行状态。 - **Token 和积分用量统计页面**：按天查看 Token 与积分消耗，支持按账号筛选，并显示模型和账号用量排行。 - **积分不足时的账号切换建议**：当前账号积分不足时提示可用账号，方便继续工作。 - **模型频率限制与预计解封时间**：检测到模型限流后，在账号页展示受限模型及预计解封时间。 - **自动化任务**：从 GitHub / Gitee 公开仓库发现并导入任务，或用自然语言让 WorkBuddy 创建任务；支持编辑、手动、事件和定时触发，以及运行日志、停止任务和 JSON / ZIP 导出。 - **权限弹窗免打扰**：真正的零决策弹窗弹出，可以放心开启任务后睡觉。 - **暂存提示词**：输入框边上一键把草稿「暂存」到待发送队列——图片 / 文件 / 引用原样保留，择机发送。 - **切换精美主题**：WorkBuddy 的「接管主题」提供跟随系统、浅色、深色、护眼绿、赛博紫、毛玻璃六种外观；「跟随系统」监听操作系统的深浅色模式变化自动切换，毛玻璃支持预设壁纸、自定义图片壁纸和视频壁纸（MP4 / WebM，静音循环、窗口切后台自动暂停），关闭接管后恢复客户端原生主题。 - **账号间会话迁移**：自动或手动跨账号复制会话，跨账号继续接龙。 - **会话分支**：在「增强」页开启后，任意一条回复都能从此处开始新会话——复制到该条回复为止的聊天内容，原会话保持不变，可在当前工作区继续聊。 - **模型切换更便捷**：解决 WorkBuddy 不支持添加多个同名模型的问题。 - **防止电脑休眠**：睡前任务未完成，开启休眠模式，任务结束后自动切换成允许休眠。 - **异常中断会话自动继续**：AI 回复因网络波动、超时等原因中断时，自动让异常中断任务继续执行。 - **快捷短语**：常用语存进面板，输入框操作栏一键点发； --- ## 客户端与功能范围 | 官方客户端 | 对应安装包品牌 | profile | | -------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | | WorkBuddy 国内版 | WorkDaddy | workbuddy-cn | | WorkBuddy AI 国际版 | WorkDaddy AI | `workbuddy-ai` | | CodeBuddy CN 国内版（Electron） | CodeDaddy CN | `codebuddy-cn` | | CodeBuddy 国际版（Electron） | CodeDaddy | `codebuddy-intl` | - 请注意：CodeBuddy 不展示「增强」页；「主题」页仅提供悬浮机器人设置。 ## 演示 ![用量统计图](docs/images/usage.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-enhance.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-robot.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-theme.png) --- ## 安装 先安装并登录上表对应的官方客户端，再下载匹配的增强工具。四款包独立安装、使用各自的账号备份目录；安装包名称中的空格使用连字符。 ### macOS 1. 在 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应的 `WorkDaddy-x.y.z.dmg`、`WorkDaddy-AI-x.y.z.dmg`、`CodeDaddy-CN-x.y.z.dmg` 或 `CodeDaddy-x.y.z.dmg` 2. 打开 DMG，把里面对应的 `.app` 拖进 **应用程序** 文件夹 3. 第一次打开如果遇到「无法打开，因为 Apple 无法检查恶意软件」： 1. 打开「系统设置 → 隐私与安全性」 2. 在「WorkDaddy 已被阻止」处点 **仍要打开** 3. 输入开机密码确认 ![安装引导](docs/images/install-guide.png) 4. 双击对应的 WorkDaddy / CodeDaddy 应用：它会启动本地守护进程，并把面板注入匹配的客户端。macOS 启动器使用本机 Node.js，建议安装 Node.js 22.13 或更新版本。 5. 看到机器人按钮？**搞定**。 #### 企业专享版 / VPC 客户端 macOS 会自动扫描带 `WorkBuddy` 前缀且包含 `Contents/MacOS/Electron` 的客户端（例如 `WorkBuddy企业定制版.app`），并按 WorkDaddy/WorkDaddy AI profile 排除另一端。发现多个候选时会弹出系统选择窗口，选中后自动记住，不需要手动寻找配置文件。完全自定义名称也可以在源码目录执行下面的高级配置命令： ```bash node scripts/workbuddy-target.js --configure --platform darwin \ --profile workbuddy-cn \ --binary "/Applications/企业客户端.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron" \ --data-dir "$HOME/Library/Application Support/WorkDaddy" ``` ### 会话工作目录恢复 默认不会自动重建已删除的会话工作目录。旧会话需要原目录时，请手动恢复目录；如需启用 Windows 上的自动恢复，可在启动 WorkDaddy 前设置环境变量 `WORKDADDY_REPAIR_MISSING_SESSION_WORKSPACES=1`。启用后，缺失目录会被定期重建。 ### Windows 1. 在 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应客户端的 `WorkDaddy-Setup-x.y.z.exe`、`WorkDaddy-AI-Setup-x.y.z.exe`、`CodeDaddy-CN-Setup-x.y.z.exe` 或 `CodeDaddy-Setup-x.y.z.exe` 2. 双击安装器完成安装 3. 双击打开对应品牌的桌面快捷方式 #### Windows 便携版 ZIP 不想安装时，可以使用对应的 `<品牌>-Portable-x.y.z.zip`：品牌为 `WorkDaddy`、`WorkDaddy-AI`、`CodeDaddy-CN` 或 `CodeDaddy`。 1. 先安装并登录对应的 WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy 客户端。 2. 将 ZIP 解压到一个有写入权限的目录，不要直接在压缩包内运行。 3. 双击解压目录顶层的 `Start-WorkDaddy.cmd`；也可以直接运行 `WorkDaddyLauncher.exe`。 4. 需要停止后台服务时，运行同目录的 `Stop-WorkDaddy.cmd`。 便携包不会创建桌面快捷方式或卸载项；账号备份和运行数据仍保存在当前用户的 `%APPDATA%\WorkDaddy`，不会随 ZIP 搬走。同一客户端 profile 不能同时运行安装版与便携版，也不能同时运行两份便携版。便携版不使用面板中的自动更新，升级时先运行 `Stop-WorkDaddy.cmd`，确认旧进程停止后再解压新版 ZIP。需要常驻安装和桌面快捷方式时，请下载对应的 Setup.exe。 #### 企业专享版 / VPC 客户端 企业专享版用户仍安装与界面最接近的 `WorkDaddy` 或 `WorkDaddy AI`。安装程序会先自动识别对应的官方客户端，并在安装向导中显示路径和版本；企业版用户点击「浏览」改选自己的 `.exe` 主程序即可，不需要修改配置文件或设置系统环境变量。 选择结果保存在 WorkDaddy 的个人数据目录中。更新安装默认保留上次选择，也可以在安装向导中修改；需要改回官方客户端时，重新运行安装程序并选择自动识别出的官方 `.exe`。WorkDaddy 会锁定所选客户端版本，客户端升级或移动后同样通过安装程序重新确认。 ### Linux Linux 发布包面向 Ubuntu / Debian `amd64` 和 `arm64`，内置对应架构的 Node.js。请先安装并登录同架构的官方客户端；增强工具通过本机调试接口连接，不修改客户端本体。 | 品牌 | DEB 文件 | 安装目录 / Debian 包名 | | ------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | | WorkDaddy | `WorkDaddy_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/workdaddy` / `workdaddy` | | WorkDaddy AI | `WorkDaddy-AI_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/workdaddy-ai` / `workdaddy-ai` | | CodeDaddy CN | `CodeDaddy-CN_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/codedaddy-cn` / `codedaddy-cn` | | CodeDaddy | `CodeDaddy_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/codedaddy` / `codedaddy` | 1. 从 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应文件，`` 为 `amd64` 或 `arm64`。 2. 在下载目录安装选中的包，例如： ```bash sudo apt install ./CodeDaddy-CN_1.2.9_amd64.deb ``` 3. 从应用菜单启动对应品牌的应用。首次启动会准备数据目录并启动后台服务；随后按提示开启客户端 CDP。CodeBuddy 请进入 Electron 智能体窗口。 四款包可以同时安装，互不覆盖，默认不设置开机自启。没有应用菜单时，可运行对应入口： ```bash bash /opt/workdaddy/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh cn bash /opt/workdaddy-ai/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh ai bash /opt/codedaddy-cn/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh codebuddy-cn bash /opt/codedaddy/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh codebuddy-intl ``` 需要开机启动后台服务时，按对应 profile 启用 systemd 用户服务，例如： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-cn bash /opt/codedaddy-cn/scripts/systemd-install-linux.sh ``` 用 `sudo apt remove <包名>` 卸载。卸载不会删除账号备份和运行数据；需要清理时，先确认 `~/.config/WorkDaddy` 中对应 profile 的数据。Linux 暂不支持面板内自动更新，请安装新版 DEB 升级。 #### 从源码安装 Linux 版本 在 Linux 主机上执行： ```bash git clone https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy.git cd WorkDaddy bash scripts/install-linux.sh bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp-linux.sh ``` 国际版 WorkBuddy AI 使用隔离环境时执行： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-ai bash scripts/workbuddy-ai-linux.sh install bash scripts/workbuddy-ai-linux.sh relaunch ``` 需要指定 WorkBuddy 可执行文件时，追加 `WBSWITCH_WORKBUDDY_BIN=/path/to/workbuddy`；安装脚本会创建备份目录、记录客户端路径并启动本地守护进程。 ### 从源码运行（开发者） ```bash git clone https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy.git cd WorkDaddy bash scripts/install.sh # 创建备份目录 + 启动守护进程 bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh # 把 WorkBuddy 切换到调试模式（端口 9222） ``` 四款客户端使用同一套 daemon，通过 profile 绑定客户端，不靠“第一个 CDP 端口”猜测目标： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-cn bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-ai bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-cn bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-intl bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh ``` macOS 发布四款 DMG；Linux 为四款客户端分别提供 `amd64`、`arm64` DEB；Windows 构建脚本为四款客户端生成 Setup.exe 和 Portable ZIP。具体可下载的平台与版本以 [Releases](../../releases) 中的资产为准。 ```bash WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 bash scripts/build-mac-dmg.sh WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 WORKDADDY_BUILD_ARCH=amd64 bash scripts/build-linux-deb.sh WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 WORKDADDY_BUILD_ARCH=arm64 bash scripts/build-linux-deb.sh ``` macOS 可用 `WORKDADDY_BUILD_PROFILE` 指定上表中的单个 profile。Windows Portable ZIP 可直接使用；`*-win64.zip` 仅为安装器构建的临时输入，不作为发布包。 `install.sh` 做了： - 创建 `~/Library/Application Support/WorkDaddy` 备份目录 - 首次启动自动兼容迁移旧版 `~/Library/Application Support/HelloBuddy/accounts` 账号备份（旧目录保留不删除） - 首次备份当前 WorkBuddy 账号 - 清理旧 launchd 注册并手动启动守护进程（不再登录自启） - 立即启动后台守护进程 - 打开管理界面 `http://127.0.0.1:47832` > 守护进程会在安装结束时手动启动；需要使用时手动启动对应的 WorkDaddy 端即可。 --- ## 原理 **CDP 注入 · 不改官方安装包** ``` ┌─────────────┐ --remote-debugging-port=9222 ┌──────────────┐ │ WorkBuddy │ <───────────────────────────> │ WorkDaddy │ │ (Electron) │ Chrome DevTools │ daemon.js │ │ │ Protocol (CDP) │ │ │ 渲染进程 │ ←── Runtime.evaluate ──── │ HTTP :47832 │ │ 右下角 │ 注入 inject.js │ 本地 API │ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ``` 以下示意图以 WorkBuddy 国内版为例；四个 profile 的默认本地 API 端口依次为 `47832`、`47833`、`47834`、`47835`，渲染器 CDP 端口依次为 `9222`、`9223`、`9224`、`9225`。CodeBuddy 另用本机主进程调试端口 `9244` / `9245` 访问原生登录态与会话存储。 1. **不修改 WorkBuddy 二进制**：用 `launcher` 启动 WorkBuddy 时多带一个 `--remote-debugging-port=9222` 参数，**二进制与签名原封不动**。 2. **守护进程通过 CDP 连接 WorkBuddy**：监听登录/认证网络事件 + 文件监听兜底，每次登录/刷新令牌都把当前登录信息按 `account.uid` 备份到稳定目录。 3. **注入界面组件**：`Runtime.evaluate` 把 `inject.js` 推到渲染进程执行，在右下角渲染机器人按钮和多标签页面板（账号 / 主题 / 会话 / 模型 / 增强 / 自动化 / 电脑 / 关于 / 设置），按客户端能力显示，CodeBuddy 隐藏「增强」。 4. **本地 HTTP API**：daemon 在 `127.0.0.1:47832` 起服务，组件通过 fetch 调用（账号切换、主题应用、成长进度查询、决策弹窗开关、休眠控制等）。 5. **数据边界清晰**：账号备份和本地配置保存在本机；按功能访问 WorkBuddy 官方 API 或 CodeBuddy 官方 API（登录、积分）和 GitHub Releases（更新检查），显式执行模型连通测试时会向你配置的模型服务发送请求及对应 API Key；脱敏错误诊断默认开启，可在「关于」页关闭。 > 为什么用 CDP 而不是官方插件机制：直接面向运行中的应用实例，事件级感知登录变化， > 主动注入界面与样式补丁，**官方升级 WorkBuddy 后只要界面没大改就照常工作**。 --- ## 使用 ### 面板 WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy Electron 窗口右下角的机器人按钮 → 弹出面板 → 选你要的操作： | Tab | 能做什么 | | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **账号** | 查看账号数、积分、模型频率限制与预计解封时间、当日签到状态、连续活跃天数、成长任务进度及 Buddy 旅行状态；切换、删除或登录新账号，并加密导入导出账号备份 | | **主题** | WorkBuddy：接管主题并选择六种外观（含跟随系统），管理壁纸、头像和背景；CodeBuddy：黑白悬浮机器人设置 | | **会话** | 按账号和时间筛选会话，批量复制或删除，并设置会话 / 工作空间在切换账号时自动复制 | | **模型** | 管理当前模型和备选模型，支持备份、复制、编辑、启用、连通测试及批量删除 | | **增强** | 配置权限免打扰、异常中断自动续接、会话分支、暂存提示词和快捷短语 | | **自动化** | 从 GitHub / Gitee 发现并导入任务、让 WorkBuddy 创建任务，管理触发方式与运行日志，以及 JSON / ZIP 导出 | | **电脑** | 允许或持续禁止休眠，也可在所有 AI 任务结束后自动恢复休眠 | | **关于** | 查看版本和项目说明、检查并安装更新、控制脱敏错误诊断 | | **设置** | 选择中文或英语；首次打开按系统语言匹配，未匹配时使用英语 | **输入框插件（仅 WorkBuddy / WorkBuddy AI）**：在「增强」页分别开启「暂存提示词」和「快捷短语」后，输入框操作栏会显示对应按钮。 暂存提示词可把当前草稿（文字、图片、文件、引用等**完整原样**）加入 WorkBuddy 自带的待发送队列，并暂停自动发送； 入队后输入框自动清空，内容按会话独立保存，可随时发送、编辑或删除。快捷短语可在增强页新增、编辑和批量管理，并从输入框操作栏一键发送，发送后不会自动删除。 ### 自动化 把重复操作保存成任务，例如查询账号积分、按条件显示提醒，或在指定会话发送消息并等待回复。 1. 打开「自动化」页，通过「发现任务」浏览公开仓库中的任务，或使用「让 WorkBuddy 帮我创建」描述需求。WorkBuddy 会在新会话中生成任务，完成后自动加入列表；「查看接口说明」提供当前支持的操作说明。 2. 设置触发方式：手动运行，或在客户端加载、打开面板、页面就绪、账号切换等事件发生时执行；也支持按间隔、每日、每周、每月或指定时间调度。 3. 在列表中启用、停用、编辑或复制任务。手动任务可立即运行，事件和定时任务按配置触发；执行过程中可停止，并通过「运行日志」查看结果和失败步骤。 **任务导入导出**：通过「发现任务」从 GitHub / Gitee 公开仓库导入，导入后保持停用，不覆盖相同 ID 的已有任务；不兼容任务会提示原因。通过批量操作选择任务导出，单个保存为 JSON，多个保存为 ZIP。 #### 提交公开任务 「发现任务」收录 GitHub 和 Gitee 公开仓库中的任务，参考示例仓库 [`babygoton/workdaddy-official-plugin`](https://github.com/babygoton/workdaddy-official-plugin)： 1. 克隆示例仓库，删掉 `tasks/` 目录里不需要的示例任务； 2. 把自己的自动化任务 JSON 放进 `tasks/` 目录（单个文件不超过 1 MiB，每个仓库最多收录 200 个）； 3. 提交改动并推送到 GitHub 或 Gitee； 4. 在仓库描述（简介）里加入关键词 `WorkDaddyAutomationRepository`。 符合约定的仓库会在下一次刷新后出现在「发现任务」列表中（搜索结果有 10 分钟缓存）。导入只读取文件并做兼容性检查，不会执行任务；导入后保持停用，相同 ID 的已有任务不会被覆盖。 任务定义保存在本机，由 WorkDaddy 本地服务执行；定时和事件触发需要服务保持运行，涉及页面交互的步骤还需要对应 WorkBuddy 客户端可用。任务导出不包含账号备份或运行日志；自动化页不提供本地 JSON / ZIP 文件导入。 ### 账号迁移到其他电脑 在账号页右上角使用「导出」和「导入」按钮即可迁移全部账号： 1. 在旧电脑打开 WorkDaddy 账号页，点击「导出」，保存生成的 `WorkDaddy-账号导出-YYYY-MM-DD.json` 文件。 2. 用安全方式把导出文件传到新电脑，并在新电脑安装、启动 WorkDaddy。 3. 打开账号页点击「导入」，选择导出文件；导入完成后即可在账号列表中切换恢复的账号。 新版导出会使用你输入的密码、每次导出随机 salt 和 AES-256-GCM 加密；密码不会写入导出文件。文件中仍包含可恢复登录状态的 token，请像保护密码一样安全保存和传输，迁移完成后及时删除不再需要的副本。旧版 v1 导出仍可兼容导入。 ## 安全与隐私 - **本地数据优先**：账号备份、主题和本地配置不会在后台上传；登录、积分等功能会访问 WorkBuddy 官方 API 或 CodeBuddy 官方 API，自动更新会访问 GitHub Releases；显式执行模型连通测试时，会向你配置的第三方模型地址发送请求及对应 API Key。 - **发送错误诊断默认开启**：关于页的「发送错误诊断」开关同时控制 Sentry 远程错误诊断和本地脱敏渲染器日志，帮助定位版本和兼容性问题；处理内容经过脱敏、截断，远程上报不包含账号、会话内容、Token 或 API Key。随时可以在关于页关闭；`WORKDADDY_TELEMETRY=0`/`1` 可作为启动时的明确关闭/开启覆盖。 独立的 `SECURITY.md` 可补充完整威胁模型；未提供时，本节即为安全与隐私说明。 --- ## 许可与声明 本项目采用 **[GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE)** 开源（`SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later`）。 - 本项目面向本机运行的 WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy 桌面端做界面与体验增强，**与两者官方无隶属关系**。 - WorkBuddy、CodeBuddy 及其商标、官方资源归其权利人所有；本项目未获得其官方授权或认可。 - 第三方主题、壁纸、背景图等素材仅作演示，商用前请自行确认权利。 --- --- ## 社区支持 [Linux.do](https://linux.do/)

repositories.description: Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini, Grok Build, Kimi Code, MiniMax Code, Muse, OMP, OpenCode, Pi, Prime Agent, etc versions of Poteto's pstack. Rigorous agent workflows with Cursor primitives translated for other harnesses.
repositories.readme:
# pstack [![Buy Me A Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20A%20Coffee-support-yellow?logo=buy-me-a-coffee&logoColor=white)](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer) [![Mentioned in Awesome Claude Code](https://awesome.re/mentioned-badge.svg)](https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code) Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Built for Claude Code This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. [Upstream's Claude Code install](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/ca782ed/harness/pstack/claude-code) asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to `poteto-mode`. ## Install ### Any harness: npm or Homebrew ```shell npx open-pstack ``` Or install it once and run it by name: ```shell npm install -g open-pstack open-pstack ``` With Homebrew: ```shell brew install michael-denyer/tap/open-pstack ``` `open-pstack` needs Node 20 or later; Homebrew installs Node for you. It finds the agent harnesses on your `PATH` and shows a picker. Press Enter to install into the ones it found, or choose others by number or id, then confirm the planned steps. It runs the same recipe as each harness's section below. | Option | Effect | | --- | --- | | `--only claude,pi` | Install into the named harnesses without the picker. Each section below gives its id. | | `--yes` | Install into every detected harness without asking. | | `--dry-run` | Print every step without running or writing anything. | | `--list` | Show each harness id and whether it was detected. | The shared `~/.agents/skills` directory (id `skills`) is never chosen by default, because Codex and OpenCode read it as well as their own plugin and would load each skill twice. Choose it for Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, or DeepSeek Harness. Muse, Grok Build, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, and the shared skills directory install from a local copy of the plugin, so no clone is needed: `open-pstack` stages the copy that ships with it at `~/.local/share/open-pstack/pstack`, or under `XDG_DATA_HOME` when that is set. To update, upgrade the installer (`npm update -g open-pstack` or `brew upgrade open-pstack`) and run `open-pstack` again. That refreshes the staged copy, so the shared skills links pick up the new version and any new skills. Plugins that a harness installed itself update through that harness, as its section below describes. See [Install with open-pstack](docs/reference.md#install-with-open-pstack) for uninstalling. ### One harness at a time
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open the **Marketplaces** tab, select `pstack-claude`, and choose **Enable auto-update**. To update once by hand, run `claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude`. Or: `npx open-pstack --only claude`.
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ``` Invoke a skill by typing `$` and its name, such as `$poteto-mode` or `$babysit`, then choosing its entry, which inserts `$pstack:`. `/skills` lists every skill. Or: `npx open-pstack --only codex`.
Pi Run in your terminal, with Pi 1.5.1 or later: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`. Or: `npx open-pstack --only pi`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected. Or: `npx open-pstack --only copilot`.
Muse Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack muse plugins approve pstack ``` The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its `SessionStart` hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with `/` (for example `/poteto-mode`), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only muse`.
OMP Run in your terminal: ```shell omp plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude omp plugin install --scope user pstack@pstack-claude ``` Restart OMP after installing, disabling, or uninstalling pstack. OMP 18.16.0 shares one plugin cache across scopes, so an upgrade or removal can affect other installations; inspect their source and scope before changing them. See [OMP issue 16827](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/16827). Or: `npx open-pstack --only omp`.
Kimi Code CLI After a release containing `kimi.plugin.json` is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session: ```text /plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude /reload ``` To test an unreleased checkout, use `/plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude` instead, followed by `/reload`; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run `/reload`. Invoke a skill as `/skill:pstack:poteto-mode`; see the [Kimi mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/kimi-tools.md) for tool guidance. `open-pstack --only kimi` prints these steps; Kimi installs plugins only from inside a session.
Grok Build ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust grok plugin enable pstack ``` Start a new session and use `/poteto-mode` to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect `grok plugin details pstack` and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run `grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data`, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. `grok plugin update` does not refresh a local install. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only grok`.
MiniMax Code For a first install, check that `${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack` does not already exist. Then run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins" cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack" ``` MiniMax Code loads each directory under `plugins/` in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. `mcode plugin list` shows it as `pstack@local`. To update, record its enabled state, quit every `mcode` process, and move `plugins/pstack` to an unused path outside `plugins/`. Run `git pull` and the `cp` line again. Check `mcode plugin list` and restore the previous enabled state if needed. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only minimax`.
OpenCode 2 Clone the repository, then add the absolute path to `plugins/pstack/opencode` to the existing `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. On Windows, use a path such as `C:/Users/name/pstack-claude/plugins/pstack/opencode`. Restart OpenCode after checkout updates. Alternatively, install, check, or update the native Git package: ```bash opencode plugin add 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin check 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin update 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' ``` A commit-pinned reference does not advance. If a check immediately after installation reports no package plugins, wait for the server to load it and check again. If you previously installed pstack skills into `~/.agents/skills`, inspect the links and remove only those pointing to your pstack checkout before using the plugin. The plugin registers `pstack-` skill IDs, registers the bundled agents as subagents under their Claude Code names, such as `pstack:poteto-agent`, and adds routing in root sessions. If routing is missing, run `opencode api get /api/skill` and check that each `pstack-` path belongs to this plugin. Resolve any conflicting skill before manually invoking that ID. Use `session hook: off` in the OpenCode model sheet to disable routing. To remove the plugin, remove its configured path and restart the service, or use `opencode plugin remove` with the exact Git specifier. OpenCode 1 is unsupported. See the [OpenCode mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/opencode-tools.md). Or: `npx open-pstack --only opencode`.
Antigravity (agy) Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack ``` This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (`skills`, `agents`, and `SessionStart` routing hook) into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack`. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only agy`.
DeepSeek Harness (skills-only) Use the [shared skills installation](#other-harnesses) below to link each pstack skill directory into `~/.agents/skills/`, which DSH discovers by default. Ask for `poteto-mode` by name and use the [DSH mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/dsh-tools.md), regardless of the model provider. This skills-only installation adds no native DSH bundle, Pi extension, routing hook, or role sheet. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only skills`.
Other harnesses Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, DeepSeek Harness skills-only installs, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")" test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target" done ``` To update, run `git pull` in the clone, then run the `for` loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for `poteto-mode` by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See [shared installation](docs/reference.md#shared-skills-installation) for per-harness notes and uninstalling. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only skills`.
### Configure pstack provides automatic routing on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, Pi, Kimi Code CLI, OMP, and OpenCode 2. The runtimes deliver the instruction at different points: Kimi adds it while the plugin is enabled, OMP adds it before each main-agent turn, and OpenCode adds it at each model step in root sessions. Grok Build exposes a routing hint through a skill description; the model may not follow it. Codex requires hook trust through `/hooks`, and Muse requires `muse plugins approve pstack`. Other harnesses have no automatic routing. Run `setup-pstack` to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (`arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max`). On OMP, the session hook setting applies globally across profiles; on Kimi, enable or disable the plugin to control routing. See the [routing reference](docs/reference.md#automatic-routing). ## Getting started ```text Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages. ``` For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses `how` and `why` to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in `architect` before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence. A localized bug with a demonstrated cause can use the [focused-fix exception](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/bug-fix.md#focused-fix-exception). One delegate investigates and implements the correction when it preserves existing interfaces and state semantics and has a focused regression check. Reproduction, verification, and required independent review still apply; a small patch alone does not qualify. [Other playbooks](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md#playbooks) cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects. ![poteto-mode on Claude Code, Codex, and Pi turns a request into verified work. Choose a playbook, plan and delegate with architect, arena, or swarm, then review and verify with interrogate, tests, and measurements. Project playbooks customize the workflow, and setup-pstack configures the model and reasoning effort per role. Supporting skills include how, why, and unslop.](assets/pstack-overview.png) ## Details - [Skills and slash commands](docs/reference.md#slash-commands) - [Runtime setup](docs/reference.md#runtime-support) - [Models and dependencies](docs/reference.md#configuration-and-dependencies) - [Maintenance and port scope](docs/reference.md#maintenance) ## Data handling pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login. This port has no automatic agent-diary reporting or diary opt-in setting. For a local decision trail, ask for [`show-me-your-work`](plugins/pstack/skills/show-me-your-work/SKILL.md). Longer or unattended workflows also invoke it. The trail stays uncommitted by default. If the trail is committed and pushed to a shared PR, anyone with access to the PR can read it. To share feedback, submit a short, manually reviewed report through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues). Include the pstack version, runtime, relevant workflow, and observed result. Remove credentials, customer data, private repository links, and sensitive log or configuration values before posting; share a summary instead of raw transcripts. ## Contributing Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). To support maintenance of this port, [buy the maintainer a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer). ## License This port, including its modifications and additions, is also [MIT-licensed](LICENSE), © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See [LICENSE-cursor-team-kit](LICENSE-cursor-team-kit), [LICENSE-thermos](LICENSE-thermos), and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

# Why Twenty Twenty gives technical teams the building blocks for a custom CRM that meets complex business needs and quickly adapts as the business evolves. Twenty is the CRM you build, ship, and version like the rest of your stack. Learn more about why we built Twenty
# Installation ### Cloud The fastest way to get started. Sign up at [twenty.com](https://twenty.com) and spin up a workspace in under a minute, with no infrastructure to manage and always up to date. ### Build an app Scaffold a new app with the Twenty CLI: ```bash npm install -g twenty twenty app init my-app cd my-app yarn install ``` Define objects, fields, and views as code: ```ts import { defineObject, FieldType } from 'twenty-sdk/define'; export default defineObject({ nameSingular: 'deal', namePlural: 'deals', labelSingular: 'Deal', labelPlural: 'Deals', fields: [ { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: FieldType.TEXT }, { name: 'amount', label: 'Amount', type: FieldType.CURRENCY }, { name: 'closeDate', label: 'Close Date', type: FieldType.DATE_TIME }, ], }); ``` Then ship it to your workspace: ```bash twenty auth login --url https://your-workspace.twenty.com twenty app publish --private ``` See the [app development guide](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/getting-started) for objects, views, agents, and logic functions. Building with a coding agent? Install the official [Twenty app skills](./packages/twenty-agent-skills), which work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and any other harness supported by the `skills` CLI: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/tree/agent-skills --list ``` The `agent-skills` branch is created by the first successful publish from `main`. Until then, use the [local build instructions](./packages/twenty-agent-skills#local-development). [`SKILLS.md`](./SKILLS.md) explains the other skill families in this repository and who they are for. ### Self-hosting Run Twenty on your own infrastructure with [Docker Compose](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/self-host/capabilities/docker-compose), or contribute locally via the [local setup guide](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/contribute/capabilities/local-setup).
